content_html:
Lets AI agents browse the web as short, numbered text instead of screenshots.

perzian.dev/mantis · by Perzian

It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or your own agent as an MCP server. Install in two commands.

npx -y -p mantis-browser mantis install
claude mcp add mantis -- npx -y -p mantis-browser mantis-mcp
npx -y -p mantis-browser mantis read https://example.com   # try it without an agent

Windows, Linux servers and other agents: SETUP.

One real task (Luna, each tool’s median run of 5 by input tokens, replayed): about half the time, over 3.5x fewer input tokens, less than half the calls. Across all 5 runs: 3-5x fewer tokens, about half the time, 11-12 calls vs 21-29. This is a selected example from 16 long tasks; medians across all 16 are in Results. Full video.

Security and threat model: SECURITY.md.

How it works

What the agent sees

Results

Mantis vs the accessibility tree (Playwright MCP) on public sites, gpt-6-luna and claude-haiku-5-5. Every cell is a per-run median; time is end-to-end wall time per run:

0.1.13: headline numbers are 0.1.9's; later builds checked on Dickens (Luna, Haiku), the capability-v1 local set and the visual-live-v1 real-site set.

Long tasks (correct: 14 keyed tasks, 42 runs per cell; medians: all 16 tasks, 48 runs per cell; both approaches run in the same session):

Luna Mantis Luna tree Haiku Mantis Haiku tree
Correct 35/42 34/42 40/42 40/42
Input tokens (median) 244k 345k 268k 506k
Tool calls (median) 17 24 19 30
Time (median) 42s 66s 54s 85s

Short tasks (30 tasks, 90 runs per cell; tree and screenshot columns are the earlier 20261026 run):

Luna Mantis Luna tree Luna screenshot Haiku Mantis Haiku tree Haiku screenshot
Correct 88/90 86/90 90/90 90/90 88/90 88/90
Input tokens (median) 64k 99k 104k 38k 88k 33k
Tool calls (median) 3 4 7 3 5 6
Time (median) 16s 31s 35s 19s 30s 23s

Versus the accessibility tree:

  • Long tasks: accuracy within one run, 29-47% fewer input tokens, 29-37% fewer calls, about a third less time.
  • Short tasks: accuracy equal or better, 35-57% fewer input tokens.

Versus screenshots:

  • Luna: screenshots score 2 runs higher but use more tokens and time.
  • Haiku: screenshots use fewer tokens.

Caveats:

  • Short-task times compare a newer Mantis build with the earlier tree and screenshot run, so treat that time gap as indicative.
  • Scores come from deterministic answer keys on the final page state. Two long iframe/tab tasks can't be keyed and are left out of the long-task counts.
  • Method and full caveats: bench/RESULTS.md.

Use your own Chrome

Optional. Mantis can drive your real Chrome (your tabs, your sign-ins) instead of launching a fresh browser:

  • Run npx -y -p mantis-browser mantis chrome. It starts Chrome on 127.0.0.1:9222 with a dedicated profile.
  • Add MANTIS_CDP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9222 to the env of the Mantis MCP config.
  • Sign in to your sites once in that profile; sign-ins persist there.
  • Mantis then acts on your real tabs, so act carefully. Without the variable nothing changes.

Limitations

  • No canvas input: canvas, WebGL, maps and drawing apps are described only as canvas, with no coordinate click or draw tool.
  • Login and bot walls need ask_human, which needs a display.
  • Benchmarked only on read, navigate and form-fill tasks on public sites, with two models. The screenshot baseline is this project's own tool, and a few tasks were swapped after results (disclosed).
  • Page content is untrusted data; see SECURITY.md.
  • Small v0.1.x beta.

Learn more

  • How it works in detail
  • Claude skill: teaches Claude how to read Mantis output
  • Install, configuration and tool reference
  • Re-running the benchmarks

License
